To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of the dipeptidase DCP from Escherichiacoli has been determined in the presence of two dipeptide "products".

the Dcp crystal structure reveals a product-bound "closed" state, which is generated from the substrate-accessible "open" form by a hinge bending mechanism, and that Dcp consists only of two subdomains, which are very similar to those of the M3 endopeptidase neurolysin.

(i) Dcp is the first M3 peptidasestructured in a product-bound form, (ii) Dcp consists of a two-chambered cavity, in which two bound dipeptides are fixed, and (iii) Dcp is a product-dependent dipeptidase, with a strict dipeptide specificity, and a broad residue specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterisation of dipeptidases and their inhibitors.
the structure and function of peptidases and their inhibitors.
the elucidation of the structure and mechanism of the Dcp peptidase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the M3 family peptidases consist of two half shell subdomains, which can adopt two alternative conformations, an open and a closed one, and that the open form can be converted to the closed form via a hinge movement mechanism.

Dcp represents a dipeptidase with an active site that resembles that of the M3 endopeptidase family, which is, however, fixed by side chains of two subdomains, which are very similar to those of the M3 family members.
Dcp represents a dipeptidase with a substrate specificity similar to ACE2, but a catalytic mechanism similar to neurolysin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Dcp, neurolysin and ACE2, and probably all M3 peptides, are members of a new peptidase family, which is characterized by a common mechanism of substrate binding and catalysis, but which has evolved from a common ancestor with the M2 peptidases by a duplication of a gene, followed by a divergence in the sequence of the duplicated half.
